text: Corestriction changes a right C-coaction into a D-valued coaction by applying the coalgebra map f:C→D to its coefficient factor: (id⊗f)ρ. The carrier module stays the same. Preservation of coproduct and counit makes this compatible with [Milne, right-comodule equations](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); this operation requires neither an inverse for f nor injectivity. Checks pass: [corestrictCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L162), [corestrictCoact_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L177).
The constructed map evaluates as the stated coefficient postcomposition.
Corestriction by the identity leaves the coaction unchanged.

This identity expresses corestriction as the original coaction followed by id⊗f. The notation lTensor means tensoring the map on the left by the identity of M, so f acts on the right coefficient factor. This is the postcomposition that preserves [Milne, right-comodule equations](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with no change of the underlying module. Checks pass: [corestrictCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L162), [corestrictCoact_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L187).
Evaluation confirms which tensor factor the coalgebra map acts on.
Successive coefficient postcompositions agree with composing the coalgebra maps.

The construction packages (id⊗f)ρ as a right D-comodule on the original module. A coalgebra map preserves the coproduct and counit, which transport both equations in [Milne, right-comodule equations](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The supplied coaction is retained explicitly through this formula; the capitalized name denotes a comodule structure, not a new carrier or an inverse-image submodule. Checks pass: [comul_lTensor_lTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L66), [counit_lTensor_lTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L77).
Coefficient postcomposition preserves the comultiplication part of the coaction law.
Coefficient postcomposition preserves the counit law.

The coaction of the explicitly selected corestricted structure evaluates to (id⊗f)(ρ(m)). This identifies the structure actually constructed, rather than merely asserting that some D-comodule exists. It is compatible with [Milne, right-comodule equations](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); the map on coefficients points from C to D, while the vector m remains in the original carrier module. Checks pass: [corestrictCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L162), [corestrictCoact_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L187).
The underlying linear map has exactly this evaluation formula.
Composition of corestrictions preserves the same coefficient direction.

This map sends (m⊗c)⊗(n⊗d) to (m⊗n)⊗cd, the coefficient-combination operation in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). Its stated scalar compatibility assumptions make multiplication bilinear, so it descends to tensor products. The helper itself needs neither a multiplicative identity nor associative multiplication; those extra laws are required only for later coherence statements. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [tensorCombine_natural](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L109).
The map has the claimed value on pure tensors.
Linear maps on carrier factors commute with the same coefficient combination.

The formula exposes the ordered coefficient product cd when two coacted tensor factors are combined. It is precisely the pure-tensor operation underlying the right-comodule tensor formula in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The swap moves the middle factors but does not reverse the coefficient multiplication; commutativity and associativity of that multiplication are unnecessary here. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_natural](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L109), [lTensor_comp_tensorCombine](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L308).
Carrier maps preserve the pure-tensor coefficient formula.
An algebra map on coefficients preserves the ordered multiplication.

Applying linear maps to the two carrier factors commutes with combining their coefficients. On pure tensors both sides give (f(m)⊗g(n))⊗cd; multilinearity extends the equality to every tensor. This is the naturality required by the tensor construction in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44), and it does not require the carrier maps to be comodule morphisms. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [tensorCoact_natural](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L282).
The pure-tensor formula identifies both sides.
For actual comodule morphisms this gives naturality of the diagonal coaction.

Combining three factors before or after reassociating their carrier tensor product agrees because (cd)e=c(de). This supplies associativity for the coefficient operation of [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The statement assumes associative multiplication but no multiplicative identity; tensor reassociation only changes parentheses, and no coefficient factors are interchanged. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_assoc_symm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L153), [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97).
The inverse reassociation satisfies the corresponding reverse formula.
The elementary formula reduces the comparison to associativity of multiplication.

Combining r⊗1 on the left with a coefficient column, then identifying R⊗M with M, gives r times that column. The calculation uses 1c=c and the tensor balancing relation. This is the left-unit compatibility underlying [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); it needs a multiplicative identity but does not require associative coefficient multiplication. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_lid_symm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L183), [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97).
At r=1, the reverse tensor-unit identification gives the same combination.
The pure-tensor formula verifies multiplication by the left identity coefficient.

Combining a coefficient column with r⊗1 on the right, then identifying M⊗R with M, gives r times the column. The calculation uses c1=c and tensor balancing. This is the right-unit compatibility underlying [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the formula retains its actual right-factor order without assuming coefficient multiplication commutative. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_rid_symm](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L206), [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97).
At r=1, the inverse right tensor-unit identification agrees with combination.
The elementary formula checks multiplication by the right identity coefficient.

The diagonal tensor coaction first coacts on both factors, then multiplies their coefficient factors in order. Thus m⊗n maps to Σ(m₀⊗n₀)⊗m₁n₁, exactly the right-comodule formula in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The bialgebra structure supplies compatibility of multiplication with coproduct and counit; neither an antipode nor commutativity of the coefficient algebra is required. Checks pass: [tensorCoact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L269), [tensorCoact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L378).
The diagonal map evaluates by applying the two component coactions and combining.
The constructed diagonal map satisfies coassociativity.

On m⊗n, the diagonal coaction combines ρ_M(m) and ρ_N(n). This explicitly implements the formula in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44), preserving the order of the two coefficient factors. The equation applies to arbitrary coaction values, which may be sums of pure tensors; it does not choose a particular expansion or require either module to have a basis. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [tensorCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L427).
Combination of individual terms multiplies the coefficients in the stated order.
The formula recovers the original tensor after applying the counit.

Tensoring two comodule morphisms gives a map that commutes with the diagonal coactions. The proof combines each morphism’s coaction compatibility with naturality of coefficient multiplication. This is the morphism part of the tensor construction in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44); the maps may be arbitrary comodule morphisms, with no injectivity or invertibility assumption. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_natural](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L109), [tensorMap_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L488).
Coefficient combination commutes with the underlying carrier maps.
The bundled tensor morphism uses exactly the tensor product of those maps.

Applying an algebra homomorphism φ to the combined coefficient equals applying it to each coefficient before combination, because φ(cd)=φ(c)φ(d). This supports the tensor coaction of [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44): substituting the bialgebra coproduct or counit gives its two structural compatibilities. Only the stated algebra-map preservation is needed, without injectivity or surjectivity. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [tensorCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L427).
The identity reduces on pure tensors to multiplicativity of φ.
The counit algebra map gives the actual diagonal-coaction counit law.

Combining coefficient columns and moving coefficients to the front agrees with the usual scalar-extension tensor comparison: (m⊗a),(n⊗b) yield ab⊗(m⊗n). This is the comparison underlying [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The value algebra A is commutative, and the right-hand tensor product is over A; no flatness or embedding of the original modules is asserted. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [endOfPoint_tensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L351).
Coefficient combination supplies the ordered product ab.
Evaluated comodule actions satisfy the corresponding scalar-extension tensor comparison.

This identity reorganizes two successive coefficient combinations into one combination over C⊗C. On elementary terms both sides produce (m⊗n)⊗(ab⊗cd), using componentwise tensor-algebra multiplication. It supplies the bookkeeping for the coassociativity calculation of [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). It requires an algebra C, but no coalgebra structure or commutativity of C. Checks pass: [tensorCombine_tmul_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L97), [tensorCoact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L378).
The elementary combination formula identifies the products on each side.
The identity supplies the actual reassociation step in diagonal coassociativity.

The diagonal tensor coaction is coassociative because the original coactions are coassociative and the bialgebra coproduct preserves multiplication. These are exactly the identities needed for the construction in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The tensor associator in the formula makes the target parenthesization explicit; this is not an assumption that differently parenthesized tensor products are definitionally equal. Checks pass: [lTensor_comp_tensorCombine](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L308), [assoc_comp_tensorCombine_rTensor_comp_tensorCombine](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L350).
The coproduct algebra map passes through coefficient multiplication.
The explicit tensor reassociation aligns the two coassociativity composites.

Applying the counit to the coefficient of the diagonal coaction gives x⊗1. After the tensor-unit identification this is x, the required counit law for [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). Multiplicativity of the counit reduces the calculation to the two original counit laws; the displayed tensor with 1 is the explicit unitor convention, not an extra coefficient. Checks pass: [lTensor_comp_tensorCombine](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L308), [tensorCoact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L269).
The counit algebra map passes through coefficient combination.
The coaction formula reduces the law to the two factors.

This packages the diagonal coaction as the tensor product comodule, using its proved coassociativity and counit laws. Its value matches [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44): multiply the right coefficient factors in their original order. The structure is explicitly selected because the same underlying tensor module can carry different coactions; the construction requires a bialgebra but no antipode. Checks pass: [tensorCoact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L378), [tensorCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L427).
The chosen coaction satisfies the first comodule axiom.
The chosen coaction satisfies the counit axiom.

The coaction of the chosen tensor-product comodule is exactly the diagonal map already constructed. This equation ties the packaged structure to the right-comodule formula of [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44); it refers to this selected structure, rather than to every possible coaction on the tensor carrier. No additional compatibility hypothesis is hidden in this defining equation. Checks pass: [tensorCoact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L269), [tensorCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L427).
The identified map has the expected formula on simple tensors.
The same map satisfies the counit law used in the structure.

The tensor product of two comodule morphisms has underlying map f⊗g and acts on m⊗n by f(m)⊗g(n). Naturality of the diagonal coaction supplies its comodule compatibility. This realizes the tensor bifunctor described in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44); both source and target use the specified diagonal tensor coactions, without requiring either morphism to be invertible. Checks pass: [tensorMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L501), [tensorMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L525).
The constructed morphism has the expected value on simple tensors.
Tensoring morphisms respects their composition.

The underlying linear map of the tensor morphism is exactly the tensor product of the two original linear maps. The construction adds a proof of coaction compatibility rather than altering that map, as required by the tensor category in [EGNO, §1.21, p.44](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The diagonal coactions on source and target are the explicitly selected structures. Checks pass: [tensorMap_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L501), [tensorMap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L507).
The underlying map sends m⊗n to f(m)⊗g(n).
Tensoring two identity morphisms gives the identity morphism.

A group-like coefficient g defines the linear map m↦m⊗g. Its equations Δ(g)=g⊗g and ε(g)=1 make this the homogeneous coaction appearing in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Here g is an element of the coefficient coalgebra, not an algebra-valued point; the module M itself need not be one-dimensional. Checks pass: [groupLike_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L84), [groupLike_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L91).
The associated comodule structure has exactly this value on vectors.
Its entire coaction map is the stated tensor-with-g map.

The construction equips M with the homogeneous coaction m↦m⊗g. The stored group-like equations give coassociativity and the counit law directly, matching the homogeneous components in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). It works over a coalgebra alone, without multiplication or an antipode, and selects a particular coaction on M rather than changing its carrier. Checks pass: [groupLike_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L84), [groupLike_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L91).
The selected structure evaluates to m⊗g.
The underlying coaction is exactly the claimed linear map.

The trivial comodule has coaction m↦m⊗1, obtained from the group-like element 1 of a bialgebra. This gives the trivial-action compatibility of [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The construction applies to any module, while the tensor unit is its special case M=R; trivial here specifies the coaction, not that the underlying module is zero. Checks pass: [trivial_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L225), [trivial_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L231).
The selected trivial coaction evaluates to m⊗1.
The full coaction map is tensoring each vector with coefficient 1.

A complex number is represented by an ordered pair of real numbers, its real and imaginary coordinates. Every pair is allowed, and two complex numbers are equal exactly when both coordinates agree. This declaration supplies the underlying objects; the familiar arithmetic, conjugation, and field structure are defined and verified separately. Compared with [Axler §1A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Complex/Basic.lean#L35).

The real number r is included in the complex plane as r+0i. Its real coordinate stays r and its imaginary coordinate is zero, making the inclusion injective. This is an exact inclusion, including negative and irrational inputs; it performs no rounding and does not extract real parts from complex inputs. Compared with [Axler Definition 1.1](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Complex/Basic.lean#L83).

The imaginary unit is the complex number with real coordinate zero and imaginary coordinate one. Its square is −1, fixing the usual orientation rather than choosing an arbitrary square root of −1. It is nonzero; unlike the auxiliary imaginary-unit symbol in a real specialization of RCLike, this complex number is nonzero. Compared with [Axler Definition 1.1](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Complex/Basic.lean#L240).

The squared modulus sends a+bi to a²+b² in the real numbers. It preserves zero, one, and multiplication, while addition has a cross term and is not preserved. The result is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at zero; it is the squared length, not the complex square (a+bi)². Compared with [Axler Chapter 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Complex/Basic.lean#L508).

The coordinate arithmetic makes the complex numbers a commutative field of characteristic zero. Every nonzero number has the reciprocal constructed from its conjugate and squared modulus. Lean additionally assigns zero as the inverse of zero; the field laws retain the nonzero condition for cancellation, so this convention does not make zero invertible. The star operation on complex numbers is ordinary conjugation: a+bi becomes a−bi. Applying it twice returns the original number, and it preserves addition and multiplication. A rational number is cast into the complex numbers by first viewing it as an exact real number and then adding zero imaginary part. The real-axis inclusion is packaged as a ring homomorphism, preserving zero, one, addition, and multiplication. Every complex number equals its real coordinate plus its imaginary coordinate times i. Both coordinates are real numbers, so they are included into ℂ before this arithmetic is performed. The formula reconstructs the original ordered pair for arbitrary signs and zero coordinates; it is an equality in ℂ, not in ℝ. The square of the concrete imaginary unit is −1. A complex number equals its conjugate exactly when its imaginary coordinate is zero. Thus the fixed points of conjugation are precisely the embedded real numbers, including negative ones and zero.
